questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that matches the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that matches the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should depend on road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 or older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead for dangers. Do not stare only at the road in front of your car. Watch for hazards and stay alert to traffic around you.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Only slow down if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones. Be ready to slow down or stop for equipment. Careful driving through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the street at marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, always yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red light. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officer directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should park within ____ inches of the curb.

options.text: Six

questions.explanation: Park no more than 18 inches from the curb. Always park where drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers which laws they must follow. They show rules about traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, parking, and special situations. These signs are usually white rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the center line.
Left of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: For a left turn on a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center line. Begin turning just before your car reaches the intersection center. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands must be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and allows you to turn safely on highways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop or turn.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look to the sides of your vehicle for traffic.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle for traffic.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or traffic meets, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If you can, move to the next lane to create a gap. If you cannot move, adjust your speed so incoming vehicles can enter traffic safely and smoothly.

questions.question: If dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever bad conditions prevent you from seeing other vehicles. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before going.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
Drive at a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed to let vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians pass. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Let cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash go first.
Let only vehicles on your right go first.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash go first.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let crossing or merging vehicles go first. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at traffic-controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When you merge onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At about the same speed as the traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At about the same speed as the traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, enter at about the same speed as the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so your car rolls away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, move back to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough room to safely pull back in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is not a right. It is a privilege that you must earn and keep.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a danger. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and hit the brakes hard.
Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in too close, take your foot off the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the car ahead without requiring hard braking or swerving into another lane.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on streets and highways?

options.text: No passing is allowed.
They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines on the road mean passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, you should consider each of the following, except:

options.text: Using your brakes.
Letting go of the steering wheel.
Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Letting go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against the back of your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another car.
